1.contenido: 1. The family, in modern times, has suffered perhaps like no other institution, the onslaught of broad, deep and rapid transformations of society and culture. Many families experience this situation while remaining faithful to the values ​​that constitute the foundation of the family institution. Others feel uncertain and discouraged about their mission, and even in a state of doubt or ignorance regarding the ultimate meaning and truth of marital and family life. Others, finally, due to different situations of injustice, are prevented from realizing their fundamental rights.

2.contenido: 2. A sign of this deep interest of the Church in the family has been the last Synod of Bishops, held in Rome from September 26 to October 25, 1980. It was a natural continuation of the previous ones. In fact, the Christian family is the first community called to announce the Gospel to the developing human person and to lead him to full human and Christian maturity, through progressive education and catechesis.

3.contenido: 3. The Church, illuminated by faith, which makes known the whole truth about the precious good of marriage and the family and about their deepest meanings, feels once again the duty to announce the Gospel, that is, the "good news", to everyone without distinction, in particular to those who are called to marriage and are preparing for it, to all husbands and fathers in the world.

4.contenido: 4. Given that God's designs on marriage and the family affect men and women in their concrete daily existence, in certain social and cultural situations, the Church, to fulfill its service, must strive to know the context within which marriage and family take place today.

5.contenido: 5. The discernment made by the Church becomes the offering of guidance, so that the truth and full dignity of marriage and the family are saved and realized.

6.contenido: 6. The situation in which the family finds itself has positive aspects and negative aspects: the former a sign of the salvation of Christ operating in the world; sign, the others, of the rejection that man opposes to the love of God.

7.contenido: 7. Living in such a world, under the pressures derived above all from the social media, the faithful have not always known how to remain immune from the obscuration of fundamental values and position themselves as a critical conscience of this family culture and as active subjects of the construction of an authentic family humanism.

8.contenido: 8. The entire Church is thus presented with the duty of profound reflection and commitment, so that the new culture that is emerging is intimately evangelized, true values are recognized, the rights of men and women are defended, and justice is promoted in the very structures of society. In this way the "new humanism" will not separate men from their relationship with God, but will lead them to it more fully.

9.contenido: 9. The injustice caused by sin - which has also penetrated deeply into the structures of today's world - and which often places obstacles in the way of the family in the full realization of itself and its fundamental rights, we must all oppose with a conversion of mind and heart, following Christ Crucified in the renunciation of one's own selfishness: such a conversion cannot fail to exert a beneficial and renewing influence even on the structures of society.

10.contenido: 10. It is in accordance with the constant tradition of the Church to accept from the cultures of the people, everything that is in a position to best express the inexhaustible riches of Christ. Only with the collaboration of all cultures will such riches be manifested more and more clearly and the Church will be able to move towards an increasingly complete and profound knowledge of the truth, which has already been given to her entirely by her Lord.

11.contenido: 11. God has created man in his image and likeness: calling him into existence through love, he has at the same time called him to love.

12.contenido: 12. The communion of love between God and men, a fundamental content of Revelation and Israel's experience of faith, finds a significant expression in the spousal alliance established between man and woman.

13.contenido: 13. The communion between God and men finds its definitive fulfillment in Christ Jesus, the Husband who loves and gives himself as Savior of humanity, uniting it to himself as his body.

14.contenido: 14. According to God's design, marriage is the foundation of the broader community of the family, since the very institution of marriage and conjugal love are ordered to the procreation and education of offspring, in which they find their crowning.

15.contenido: 15. In marriage and in the family, a set of interpersonal relationships is constituted – marital relationship, paternity-maternity, filiation, fraternity – through which every human person is introduced into the “human family” and the “family of God”, which is the Church.

16.contenido: 16. Virginity and celibacy for the Kingdom of God not only do not contradict the dignity of marriage, but rather presuppose and confirm it. Marriage and virginity are two ways of expressing and living the only Mystery of God's Covenant with his people. When marriage is not esteemed, consecrated virginity cannot exist either; When human sexuality is not considered a great value donated by the Creator, renunciation for the Kingdom of heaven loses meaning.

17.contenido: 17. In the plan of God the Creator and Redeemer the family discovers not only its "identity", what it "is", but also its "mission", what it can and must "do". The task that she is called to play in history by God's vocation springs from her very being and represents her dynamic and existential development. Every family discovers and finds in itself the indelible call, which defines both its dignity and its responsibility: family, "be" what you "are"!

18.contenido: 18. The family, founded and vivified by love, is a community of people: of the husband and wife, of parents and children, of relatives. Its first task is to faithfully live the reality of communion with the constant effort to develop an authentic community of people.

19.contenido: 19. The first communion is the one that is established and develops between the spouses; By virtue of the covenant of conjugal love, man and woman "are no longer two, but one flesh" and are called to continually grow in their communion through daily fidelity to the marital promise of total reciprocal self-giving.

20.contenido: 20. Marital communion is characterized not only by its unity, but also by its indissolubility: "This intimate union, as a mutual gift of two people, as well as the good of children, demand the full fidelity of the spouses and demand their indissoluble unity."

21.contenido: 21. Conjugal communion constitutes the foundation on which the broadest communion of the family, of parents and children, of brothers and sisters among themselves, of relatives and other family members, is built.

22.contenido: 22. The family, as it is and must always be a communion and community of people, finds in love the source and incessant stimulus to welcome, respect and promote each of its members in the highest dignity of persons, that is, of living images of God. As the Synod Fathers have rightly stated, the moral criterion of the authenticity of conjugal and family relationships consists of the promotion of the dignity and vocation of each person, who achieve their fullness through the sincere gift of themselves.

23.contenido: 23. Without now going into the different aspects of the broad and complex issue of women-society relations, but limiting ourselves to some essential points, one cannot fail to observe how in the more specifically family field a broad and widespread social and cultural tradition has wanted to reserve for women only the task of wife and mother, without adequately opening them up to public functions, generally reserved for men.

24.contenido: 24. Unfortunately, the Christian message about the dignity of women finds opposition in the persistent mentality that considers the human being not as a person, but as a thing, as an object of sale, at the service of selfish interest and only pleasure; The first victim of such a mentality is the woman.

25.contenido: 25. Within the conjugal and family communion-community, man is called to live his gift and his role as husband and father.

26.contenido: 26. In the family, a community of people, very special attention must be reserved for the child, developing a deep esteem for their personal dignity, as well as great respect and generous service for their rights. This applies to all children, but it takes on a special urgency when the child is small and needs everything, is sick, delicate or handicapped.

27.contenido: 27. There are cultures that express a singular veneration and great love for the elderly; Far from being separated from the family or being carried like a useless weight, the elderly remains inserted in family life, continues to take an active and responsible part - even having to respect the autonomy of the new family - and above all develops the precious mission of witness to the past and inspirer of wisdom for the young and for the future.

28.contenido: 28. God, with the creation of man and woman in his image and likeness, crowns and brings to perfection the work of his hands; He calls them to a special participation in his love and at the same time in his power as Creator and Father, through their free and responsible cooperation in the transmission of the gift of human life: "And God blessed them and said to them: "Be fruitful and multiply and replenish the earth and subdue it."

29.contenido: 29. Precisely because the love of spouses is a unique participation in the mystery of life and the love of God himself, the Church knows that it has received the special mission of guarding and protecting the highest dignity of marriage and the very serious responsibility of the transmission of human life.

30.contenido: 30. The doctrine of the Church today finds itself in a social and cultural situation that makes it both more difficult to understand and more urgent and irreplaceable in promoting the true good of men and women.

31.contenido: 31. The Church is certainly also aware of the multiple and complex problems that today, in many countries, affect spouses in their task of responsibly transmitting life. He also knows the serious problem of demographic increase as it arises in various parts of the world, with the moral implications that it entails.

32.contenido: 32. In the context of a culture that seriously distorts or even loses the true meaning of human sexuality, because it uproots it from its reference to the person, the Church feels more urgent and irreplaceable its mission to present sexuality as the value and function of the entire created person, male and female, in the image of God.

33.contenido: 33. Also in the field of marital morality the Church is and acts as Teacher and Mother.

34.contenido: 34. It is always very important to have a correct conception of the moral order, its values and norms; The importance increases the more numerous and serious the difficulties in respecting them become.

35.contenido: 35. Faced with the problem of honest regulation of birth rates, the ecclesial community, in the present time, must be concerned with raising convictions and offering concrete help to those who wish to live fatherhood and motherhood in a truly responsible way.

36.contenido: 36. The educational task has its roots in the primary vocation of spouses to participate in the creative work of God; They, engendering in love and through love a new person, who has within them the vocation to growth and development, therefore assume the obligation to effectively help them to live a fully human life. As the Second Vatican Council has recalled: «Since parents have given life to their children, they have the very serious obligation to educate their offspring, and therefore they must be recognized as the first and main educators of their children. This duty of family education is of such importance that, when it is missing, it can hardly be replaced. It is, therefore, the duty of parents to create a family environment animated by love, by piety towards God and towards men, which favors the integral personal and social education of their children. The family is, therefore, the first school of social virtues, which all societies need.

37.contenido: 37. Even in the midst of the difficulties, often aggravated today, of educational action, parents must educate their children with confidence and courage in the essential values ​​of human life. Children must grow up in fair freedom from material goods, adopting a simple and austere lifestyle, convinced that "a man is worth more for what he is than for what he has."

38.contenido: 38. For Christian parents, the educational mission, based as has been said on their participation in the creative work of God, has a new and specific source in the sacrament of marriage, which consecrates them to the properly Christian education of their children, that is, calls them to participate in the same authority and the same love of God the Father and of Christ the Shepherd, as well as the maternal love of the Church, and enriches them in wisdom, counsel, strength and in the other gifts of the Holy Spirit, to help their children in their human and Christian.

39.contenido: 39. The mission of education requires that Christian parents offer their children all the content that is necessary for the gradual maturation of their personality from a Christian and ecclesial point of view. They will therefore follow the educational lines mentioned above, seeking to show their children to what deep meanings the faith and charity of Jesus Christ lead. Furthermore, the awareness that the Lord entrusts to them the growth of a child of God, of a brother of Christ, of a temple of the Holy Spirit, of a member of the Church, will encourage Christian parents in their task of strengthening the gift of divine grace in the souls of their children.

40.contenido: 40. The family is the first, but not the only and exclusive, educating community; The same community, civil and ecclesial dimension of man demands and leads to a broader and more articulated action, the result of the ordered collaboration of the various educational forces. These are necessary, although each one can and must intervene with their own competence and contribution.

41.contenido: 41. Fertile conjugal love is expressed in a service to life that has many forms, of which generation and education are the most immediate, proper and irreplaceable. In reality, each act of true love for man witnesses and perfects the spiritual fruitfulness of the family, because it is obedience to the inner and profound dynamism of love, as a gift of oneself to others.

42.contenido: 42. "The Creator of the world established conjugal society as the origin and foundation of human society"; The family is therefore the "first and vital cell of society."

43.contenido: 43. The same experience of communion and participation, which should characterize the daily life of the family, represents its first and fundamental contribution to society.

44.contenido: 44. The social function of the family certainly cannot be reduced to procreative and educational action, although it finds its first and irreplaceable form of expression in it.

45.contenido: 45. The intimate connection between the family and society, in the same way that it requires the openness and participation of the family in society and in its development, also requires that society not fail to fulfill its fundamental duty to respect and promote the family itself.

46.contenido: 46. The ideal of a reciprocal action of support and development between the family and society often clashes, and to a quite serious extent, with the reality of their separation and even their opposition.

47.contenido: 47. The social function of each family is the responsibility, by a new and original title, of the Christian family, founded on the sacrament of marriage. This sacrament, assuming the human reality of conjugal love in all its implications, enables and commits Christian spouses and parents to live their vocation as lay people, and consequently to "seek the kingdom of God by managing temporal affairs and ordering them according to God."

48.contenido: 48. Given the global dimension that today characterizes various social problems, the family sees its role in the development of society expanding in a totally new way; It is also about cooperating to establish a new international order, because only with global solidarity can the enormous and dramatic problems of justice in the world, the freedom of peoples and the peace of humanity be faced and resolved.

49.contenido: 49. Among the fundamental tasks of the Christian family is the ecclesial one, that is, it is placed at the service of the building of the Kingdom of God in history, through participation in the life and mission of the Church.

50.contenido: 50. The Christian family is called to take a living and responsible part in the mission of the Church in its own and original way, that is, putting its own being and actions at the service of the Church and society, as an intimate community of life and love.

51.contenido: 51. Since it participates in the life and mission of the Church, which religiously listens to the Word of God and proclaims it with firm confidence, the Christian family lives its prophetic mission by welcoming and announcing the Word of God. Thus, every day it becomes more of a believing and evangelizing community.

52.contenido: 52. To the extent that the Christian family welcomes the Gospel and matures in faith, it becomes an evangelizing community. Let us listen again to Paul VI: «The family, like the Church, must be a space where the Gospel is transmitted and from where it radiates.

53.contenido: 53. The ministry of evangelization of Christian parents is original and irreplaceable and assumes the typical characteristics of family life, made, as it should be, of love, simplicity, concreteness and daily witness.

54.contenido: 54. Universality without borders is the proper horizon of evangelization, internally animated by missionary zeal, since it is in fact the response to the explicit and unequivocal slogan of Christ: "Go into the world and preach the Gospel to every creature."

55.contenido: 55. The announcement of the Gospel and its reception through faith find their fullness in the sacramental celebration. The Church, a believing and evangelizing community, is also a priestly people, that is, clothed in the dignity and participant in the power of Christ, High Priest of the new and eternal Alliance.

56.contenido: 56. Original source and means of sanctification for spouses and for the Christian family is the sacrament of marriage, which presupposes and specifies the sanctifying grace of baptism. By virtue of the mystery of the death and resurrection of Christ, in which Christian marriage is once again situated, conjugal love is purified and sanctified: "The Lord has deigned to heal this love, perfect it and elevate it with the special gift of grace and charity."

57.contenido: 57. The duty of sanctification of the Christian family has its first root in baptism and its maximum expression in the Eucharist, to which Christian marriage is closely linked. The Second Vatican Council wanted to highlight the special relationship between the Eucharist and marriage, asking that it be usually celebrated "within the Mass." Rediscovering and deepening such a relationship is absolutely necessary if we want to understand and live with greater intensity the grace and responsibilities of marriage and the Christian family.

58.contenido: 58. An essential and permanent part of the sanctification task of the Christian family is the acceptance of the evangelical call to conversion, addressed to all Christians who do not always remain faithful to the "newness" of baptism that has made them "saints." Nor is the family always consistent with the law of grace and baptismal sanctity, proclaimed again in the sacrament of marriage.

59.contenido: 59. The Church prays for the Christian family and educates it so that it lives in generous coherence with the gift and priestly role received from Christ the High Priest. In reality, the baptismal priesthood of the faithful, lived in the marriage-sacrament, constitutes for the spouses and the family the foundation of a vocation and a priestly mission, through which their very daily existence is transformed into "a spiritual sacrifice acceptable to God through Jesus Christ." This happens not only with the celebration of the Eucharist and the other sacraments or with the offering of oneself for the glory of God, but also with the life of prayer, with the supplicating dialogue directed to the Father through Jesus Christ in the Holy Spirit.

60.contenido: 60. By virtue of their dignity and mission, Christian parents have the specific duty to educate their children in prayer, to progressively introduce them to the discovery of the mystery of God and personal conversation with Him: "Above all in the Christian family, enriched with the grace and duties of the sacrament of marriage, it is important that children learn from their earliest years to know and adore God and to love their neighbor according to the faith received in baptism."

61.contenido: 61. There is a deep and vital relationship between the prayer of the Church and that of each of the faithful, as the Second Vatican Council has clearly confirmed. An important purpose of the prayer of the domestic Church is to constitute for children the natural introduction to the liturgical prayer proper to the entire Church, in the sense of preparing it and extending it to the sphere of personal, family and social life. From this derives the need for a progressive participation of all members of the Christian family in the Eucharist, especially on Sundays and holidays, and in the other sacraments, particularly those of the Christian initiation of children. The conciliar guidelines have opened a new possibility for the Christian family, which has been placed among the groups to which the community celebration of the Divine Office is recommended. Christian families will also take care to celebrate, even at home and in a manner appropriate to their members, the times and festivities of the liturgical year.

62.contenido: 62. We must never forget that prayer is a constitutive and essential part of the Christian life considered in its integrity and depth. Furthermore, it belongs to our own "humanity" and is "the first expression of the inner truth of man, the first condition of the authentic freedom of the spirit."

63.contenido: 63. The Church, a prophetic, priestly and royal people, has the mission of leading all men to accept the Word of God with faith, to celebrate and profess it in the sacraments and in prayer, and finally to manifest it in concrete life according to the gift and the new commandment of love.

64.contenido: 64. Animated and sustained by the new commandment of love, the Christian family lives welcoming, respecting, and serving each man, always considered in his dignity as a person and as a child of God.

65.contenido: 65. Like every living reality, the family is also called to develop and grow. After the preparation during the courtship and the sacramental celebration of marriage, the couple begins the daily path towards the progressive implementation of the values ​​and duties of marriage itself.

66.contenido: 66. In our days it is more necessary than ever to prepare young people for marriage and family life. In some countries it is still the families themselves that, according to ancient customs, transmit to young people the values ​​related to married and family life through a progressive work of education or initiation. But the changes that have occurred in almost all modern societies demand that not only the family, but also society and the Church be committed to the effort of adequately preparing young people for the responsibilities of their future. Many negative phenomena that are lamented today in family life derive from the fact that, in new situations, young people not only lose sight of the correct hierarchy of values, but, no longer possessing secure criteria for behavior, they do not know how to face and resolve new difficulties. Experience teaches, however, that young people who are well prepared for family life generally do better than others.

67.contenido: 67. Christian marriage requires as a rule a liturgical celebration, which expresses in a social and community manner the essentially ecclesial and sacramental nature of the marital pact between the baptized.

68.contenido: 68. Precisely because in the celebration of the sacrament special attention is reserved for the moral and spiritual dispositions of the couple, specifically their faith, we must face here a fairly frequent difficulty, which the pastors of the Church may encounter in the context of our secularized society.

69.contenido: 69. Pastoral care of the normally constituted family means concretely the commitment of all the elements that make up the local ecclesial community in helping the couple discover and live their new vocation and mission. For the family to become increasingly a true community of love, it is necessary that its members be helped and trained in their responsibility in the face of new problems that arise, in reciprocal service, in active participation in family life.

70.contenido: 70. The Church, a community at the same time saved and saving, must be considered here in its double universal and particular dimension. This is expressed and carried out in the diocesan community, pastorally divided into smaller communities among which the parish is distinguished by its peculiar importance.

71.contenido: 71. But above all we must recognize the unique position that, in this field, corresponds to Christian spouses and families, by virtue of the grace received in the sacrament. Its mission must be put at the service of the building of the Church and the construction of the Kingdom of God in history. This is a demand for docile obedience to Christ the Lord. He, in fact, by virtue of the marriage of the baptized elevated to a sacrament, confers on Christian spouses a peculiar mission of apostles, sending them as workers to his vineyard, and, in a special way, to this field of the family.

72.contenido: 72. Without leaving the scope of the Church, the subject responsible for family pastoral care, we must remember the various groups of faithful, in which the mystery of the Church of Christ is manifested and lived in some way. Consequently, the various ecclesial communities, groups and movements committed in different ways, by titles and at different levels, in family pastoral care must be recognized and valued – each one according to its characteristics, purposes, incidences and methods.

73.contenido: 73. The first person responsible for family pastoral care in the diocese is the bishop. As a Father and Pastor, he must pay particular attention to this undoubtedly priority sector of pastoral care. You must dedicate interest, attention, time, people, resources to it; and above all personal support to the families and to those, in the various diocesan structures, who help in the pastoral care of the family. He will particularly ensure that the diocese itself becomes increasingly a true "diocesan family", a model and source of hope for so many families that belong to it. The creation of the Pontifical Council for the Family must be seen in this context; It is a sign of the importance that I attribute to the pastoral care of the family in the world, so that at the same time it is an effective instrument to help promote it at all levels.

74.contenido: 74. The help that men and women religious and consecrated souls in general can give to the apostolate of the family finds its first, fundamental and original expression precisely in their consecration to God: "In this way they evoke before all the faithful that wonderful union, founded by God and which is to be fully revealed in the future century, through which the Church has Christ as her only husband." This consecration makes them witnesses of that universal charity that, through the chastity embraced by the Kingdom of heaven, makes them increasingly available to generously dedicate themselves to divine service and works of apostolate.

75.contenido: 75. No little help can be provided to families by specialized lay people ( [+[0]+] ) who, both individually and through various associations and initiatives, offer their work of enlightenment, advice, guidance and support. The exhortations that I addressed to the Confederation of Family Consultants of Christian inspiration can be applied to them: "Yours is a commitment that well deserves the classification of mission, because of how noble the purposes it pursues are, and the results that derive from them are decisive for the good of society and of the Christian community itself... Everything that you manage to do in support of the family is destined to have an effectiveness that, going beyond its scope, also reaches other people and affects society. "The future of the world and the Church passes through the family."

76.contenido: 76. A separate word must be reserved for this category that is so important in modern life. It is known that social communication instruments "often have a profound impact, both emotionally and intellectually and morally and religiously, on the minds of those who use them," especially if they are young. Such media can exert a beneficial influence on the life and customs of the family and on the education of children, but at the same time they also hide "not insignificant pitfalls and dangers", and could become a vehicle - sometimes skilfully and systematically manipulated, as unfortunately happens in various countries of the world - of divisive ideologies and distorted visions of life, of the family, of religion, of morality and that They respect the true dignity and destiny of man.

77.contenido: 77. An even more generous, intelligent and prudent pastoral commitment is necessary, following the example of the Good Shepherd, towards those families that âoften and independently of their own will, or pressed by other demands of a different natureâ have to face objectively difficult situations.

78.contenido: 78. The growing number of marriages between Catholics and other baptized people also requires particular pastoral attention in light of the guidelines and norms contained in the recent documents of the Holy See and those prepared by the Episcopal Conferences, to facilitate their concrete application in various situations.

79.contenido: 79. In its request to protect the family in all its dimensions, not just the religious one, the Synod has not failed to carefully consider some irregular situations, from a religious and often also a civil point of view, which â€œwith the current and rapid cultural transformationsâ€ are unfortunately spreading also among Catholics with no slight damage to the family institution itself and to society, of which it is the fundamental cell.

80.contenido: 80. A first irregular situation is that of the so-called "trial marriage" or experimental, which many today want to justify, attributing a certain value to it. Human reason itself already hints at its non-acceptability, indicating that it is unconvincing to carry out an "experiment" in the case of human persons, whose dignity demands that they always and only be the term of a self-giving love, without any limit of time or other circumstances.

81.contenido: 81. These are unions without any publicly recognized institutional link, neither civil nor religious. This phenomenon, increasingly frequent, must draw the attention of pastors of souls, since there may be various elements acting on which it will perhaps be possible to limit its consequences.

82.contenido: 82. The case of Catholics who, for ideological and practical reasons, prefer to contract only a civil marriage, rejecting or, at least, deferring a religious one, is increasingly common. Their situation cannot simply be equated to that of those who live together without any ties, since there is at least a certain commitment to a specific and perhaps stable state of life, although sometimes the prospect of a possible divorce is not foreign to this situation. Seeking public recognition of the bond by the State, such couples demonstrate a willingness to assume, along with the advantages, also the obligations. Despite everything, this situation is not acceptable to the Church either. Pastoral action will try to make understood the need for coherence between the choice of life and the faith that is professed, and will try to do everything possible to convince these people to regulate their own situation in the light of Christian principles. Even if they treat them with great charity and interest them in the life of their respective communities, the pastors of the Church will not be able to admit them to the use of the sacraments.

83.contenido: 83. Various reasons, such as mutual misunderstanding, inability to open up to interpersonal relationships, etc., can painfully lead a valid marriage to a breakup that is often irreparable. Obviously separation must be considered as an extreme remedy, after any reasonable attempt has been futile.

84.contenido: 84. Daily experience teaches, unfortunately, that those who have resorted to divorce normally have the intention of moving on to a new union, obviously without the Catholic religious rite. Being a plague that, like others, increasingly invades even Catholic environments, the problem must be faced with urgent attention. The Synod Fathers have expressly studied it. The Church, in fact, established to lead all men to salvation, especially the baptized, cannot abandon to themselves those who, already united with the sacramental marriage bond, have attempted to remarry. Therefore he will tirelessly try to put the means of salvation at their disposal.

85.contenido: 85. I wish to add a word in favor of a category of people who, due to the concrete situation in which they live – often not by deliberate will – I consider especially close to the Heart of Christ, worthy of the affection and active concern of the Church, as well as of the pastors.

86.contenido: 86. To you husbands, to you fathers and mothers of families.
